access_evidence: GET https://www.importyeti.com/ returned HTTP 200 (53,134 B). robots.txt (HTTP 200, 167 B) allows crawling of pages but disallows every data endpoint: 'Disallow: /search?q', 'Disallow: /api/addresses', 'Disallow: /api/ep', 'Disallow: /cdn-cgi/', 'Disallow: /mx/', 'Disallow: /us-export/', 'Disallow: /partnerships/'. The /policies page returned 200 but no automated-access prohibition could be extracted from it (the served HTML is largely stylesheet and script text).
blockers: NO_PUBLISHED_API_LICENCE: no reusable dataset or API terms were found.
licence_note: robots.txt is the operative published restriction: 'Allow: /' followed by 'Disallow: /api/addresses' and 'Disallow: /api/ep'. The shipment data is served through exactly those disallowed paths, so a compliant crawler cannot obtain it. No explicit written reuse licence was found.
machine_interface: web pages only; internal /api/* endpoints exist but are disallowed
name: ImportYeti — US import bill-of-lading search
notes: No page was crawled beyond the homepage, robots.txt and /policies.
rate_policy: No published API; robots restricts the data endpoints.
unlock_route: Only with the operator's written permission or a commercial agreement. Absent that, company-level US customs shipment data must not be acquired from this vendor. For an aggregate alternative see un_comtrade / us_census_trade (country totals) — but those cannot substitute for company-level attribution.
what_is_new: Nothing collected, and nothing may be collected: the operator's robots policy disallows the data endpoints. This is the correct conclusion, not a workaround.
